title: AI thermal-camera early warning stops trains for elephants at Madukkarai, Tamil Nadu
summary: TN Forest Dept AI cameras on a 7.05 km rail stretch: 7,116+ alerts, thousands of train stops, zero elephant deaths since Feb 2024.
account: The Tamil Nadu Forest Department installed 24 hybrid thermal cameras with AI detection on 12 towers. They cover 7.05 km of the Ettimadai–Walayar railway section in Madukkarai forest range, Coimbatore district. They have operated since 9 February 2024. A trial run already generated alerts by 7 January 2024. Alerts go to a control room at Puthupathi. Its staff warn station masters and loco pilots and drive elephants away from the tracks. By 7 July 2026 the department's Additional Chief Secretary reported over 7,116 alerts and 3,281 train slow-downs or stops (DT Next reports 3,821). It also gave about 9,481 safe elephant crossings and no elephant deaths on the stretch. Eleven elephants were killed there between 2008 and 2022.
purpose: Detect elephants near railway tracks with thermal cameras and AI, alert forest staff and railway crews, and prevent train-elephant collisions.
system: AI-based elephant early warning system (24 hybrid thermal cameras on 12 towers, Elephant Control and Command Center, Puthupathi)
deployer: Tamil Nadu Forest Department (Department of Environment, Climate Change and Forests), with railway station masters at Walayar and Ettimadai and loco pilots
taxonomy_note: The collisions avoided are between trains and elephants, so the gain is shared with conservation.

ratings.reason: Unassessed: the reports count train stops and crossings, not injuries avoided by crews or passengers.
The Forest Department reports zero elephant deaths on a stretch that recorded eleven deaths from 2008 to 2022, including three in November 2021.

Reported 9,481 safe crossings and no track deaths for wild elephants on a stretch that recorded eleven deaths from 2008 to 2022. Counterfactual per crossing is unproven, so not rated population-level.

ai_role.statement: AI classification of thermal-camera feeds generated the alerts that triggered staff intervention and train slow-downs. The figures (alerts, stops, crossings, zero deaths) are the department's own statements as reproduced verbatim in news reports. No official document is among the sources. No per-event counterfactual is established.

paired_incident.title: Poachers Evaded AI Cameras and Killed Four Rhinos
paired_incident.basis: AI wildlife-reserve cameras failed to detect intruders and four rhinos were killed; Madukkarai's thermal cameras are the same detection-to-alert design protecting elephants.

headline: AI thermal cameras stop trains for elephants at Madukkarai
metric: about 9,481 safe elephant crossings and no elephant deaths on the stretch

comparator.against: the same 7.05 km Madukkarai railway stretch before the cameras (2008 to 2022)
comparator.before: Eleven wild elephants were killed on railway tracks in Madukkarai stretch from 2008 to 2022
comparator.after: no elephant deaths on the railway tracks in the last 22 months (as of 21 December 2025)
comparator.quote: Eleven wild elephants were killed on railway tracks in Madukkarai stretch from 2008 to 2022 with the last being reported in November 2021 when three elephants died.

later.note: At two and a half years the department reported about 9,481 safe crossings and still no elephant deaths on the stretch, and had added AI-powered drones to extend surveillance beyond the fixed cameras.
later.quote: "These are the unsung heroes whose constant vigilance, dedication, and hard work have facilitated around 9,481 safe elephant crossings, ensuring zero elephant deaths on railway tracks and demonstrating how technology, human vigilance, and teamwork can come together to protect wildlife," said Supriya Sahu.
